takeaways: Chip design turns an idea into a complete blueprint, and a chip factory accepts only designs that have passed software from Synopsys, Cadence or Siemens.
Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA took more than 85 percent of the $18 billion market for design software and licensed blocks in 2025.
The three design flows do not mix, and each foundry certifies exact tool versions, so a newcomer would have to write a fourth flow from nothing.
In 2025 Washington cut off design-software sales to China for five weeks, and China still cannot finish a leading-edge design without foreign tools.

quiz.q: What does the chip design stage produce before any factory work begins?
options: A finished set of wafers, tested and ready to be cut into separate chips
A complete blueprint fixing where each transistor sits and how it is wired
A supply contract that reserves a share of a foundry's capacity for years
A small batch of test chips printed on older and cheaper factory equipment
quiz.why: Design turns an idea into a complete blueprint, all of it in software. A chip factory accepts only designs that have passed the tools from Synopsys, Cadence or Siemens.

quiz.q: What share of the market for design software and licensed blocks did Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA hold in 2025?
options: About 40 percent
About 55 percent
About 70 percent
More than 85 percent
quiz.why: The market was worth $18 billion in 2025, and the three firms took more than 85 percent of it. No other vendor held more than 5 percent in any core category.

quiz.q: Why can a chip team not combine tools from different design-software vendors?
options: The foundry certifies exact tool versions and accepts timing signed off only in its approved tool
Each vendor's license forbids customers from buying any product sold by a rival vendor
The tools run only on computers built and sold by the same software vendor
Export law requires every chip design to use software from a single country
quiz.why: The foundry certifies its reference recipes against specific tool versions. Timing signed off in one vendor's tool is not accepted in another, so each team commits to one complete flow.

quiz.q: What followed when the United States stopped design-software sales to China in 2025?
options: Chinese designers moved to a complete domestic flow within weeks
The ban stayed in place and was widened to cover all of Asia
Sales resumed after five weeks, and China still lacks a complete domestic flow
European vendors replaced the American tools for Chinese customers
quiz.why: The letters arrived on 23 and 29 May 2025 and were rescinded on 2 July after trade talks. CSET finds that Chinese vendors cannot yet support designs at the leading edge.

takeaways: Every leading-edge chip starts on a 300 mm wafer, a slice of one silicon crystal polished flat enough for extreme-ultraviolet printing to stay in focus across the disc.
Five firms in Japan, Taiwan, Germany and South Korea make these wafers, and none of them is American or Chinese.
Switching wafer suppliers takes two to five years, because a fab must approve each new source separately for every chip it makes.
China made about 93 percent of the world's polysilicon in 2023, but 98 percent of it was solar grade and too impure for chips.

quiz.q: Why does the flatness of a wafer matter so much for leading-edge chips?
options: Flat wafers weigh less, so they cost less to ship between the plants that process them
Polishing removes the boron that doping adds, which would otherwise short the chip
Extreme-ultraviolet printing stays in focus over only a very small range of heights
Fabs stack the wafers directly on top of each other during every processing step
quiz.why: Extreme-ultraviolet printing stays in focus over only a very small range of heights. Flatness therefore has to hold at every point across a 300 mm disc.

quiz.q: Which group of firms makes the 300 mm wafers used for leading-edge chips?
options: Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, GlobalWafers, Siltronic and SK Siltron
Wacker, Hemlock, OCI, Tokuyama and Mitsubishi
Linde, Air Liquide, Air Products, Nippon Sanso and Messer
TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SMIC and SK Hynix
quiz.why: CSET names these five wafer makers, headquartered in Japan, Taiwan, Germany and South Korea. Wacker, Hemlock, OCI, Tokuyama and Mitsubishi make the electronic-grade polysilicon the wafers start from.

quiz.q: Why does switching to a new wafer supplier take two to five years?
options: Only one plant in the world can grow 300 mm crystals of this quality
Governments set wafer prices and volumes through yearly national quotas
New wafer plants may legally be built only in Japan and Germany
A fab approves each new source separately for every chip it makes
quiz.why: Each approval test runs for months, and supply contracts are signed years ahead. A new plant can be built, as GlobalWafers showed in Texas, so approval is the slow part.

quiz.q: China made about 93 percent of the world's polysilicon in 2023. Why does that give it little hold over chip wafers?
options: Chinese law allows its polysilicon to be sold only inside China
About 98 percent of that output was solar grade, too impure for chips
Chip wafers no longer use polysilicon as their starting material
Its polysilicon plants closed after US export controls took effect
quiz.why: Solar-grade material was 98 percent of China's 2023 output and electronic grade 2 percent. As of 2021 Chinese firms held under 1 percent of the 300 mm wafer market.

takeaways: Photoresist is the light-sensitive coating that holds the printed pattern on the wafer, and a few hundred other gases and liquids deposit, strip and clean layers between steps.
Japan made about 90 percent of the world's photoresist in 2021 and 78 percent in 2023.
Each resist formula is approved for one layer of one product at one fab, so Korea needed five years to build substitutes after Japan's 2019 export licenses.
China's export controls fall on gallium, germanium and antimony, which go into optics and non-silicon chips and stay out of a silicon GPU.

quiz.q: What does photoresist do in chipmaking?
options: It holds the printed pattern so the next machine can etch it into the wafer
It cools the wafer while the scanner exposes each patch of the surface
It supplies the pure metal that forms the wiring on top of the chip
It grinds each new layer flat before the next layer goes on
quiz.why: Light changes the resist where it lands, a wash removes the exposed parts, and the remaining pattern guides the etch. Sputtering targets supply the wiring metal, and polishing slurries flatten each layer.

quiz.q: Which country makes most of the world's semiconductor photoresist?
options: The United States
China
Japan
Germany
quiz.why: Japan made about 90 percent in 2021 and 78 percent in 2023. In 2023 the United States held 13 percent and South Korea 6 percent, with China inside the small remainder.

quiz.q: Why did Korea need five years to replace Japanese photoresist after Japan's 2019 export licenses?
options: Korea first had to build its own extreme-ultraviolet scanners
Each resist formula must be approved for one layer of one product at one fab
Japanese patents blocked every other resist maker until 2024
Korean fabs stopped production until domestic plants were finished
quiz.why: Qualification ties a resist to one layer of one product at one fab, so a new supplier works through the fab one layer at a time. Korea kept its fabs running while it funded substitutes.

quiz.q: Why do China's controls on gallium and germanium do little to stop silicon GPU production?
options: The United States mines enough of both metals for its own fabs
Beijing lifted both controls permanently in November 2025
Chip fabs recycle all the gallium and germanium they use
Neither metal goes into a silicon logic chip
quiz.why: Germanium goes into fiber optics, infrared optics and satellite solar cells, and gallium into the non-silicon wafers behind radio front ends, LEDs and lasers. The controls moved prices instead.

takeaways: Lithography prints each layer of a circuit onto the wafer, and finer lines need shorter light, so the finest layers need extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) scanners working in a vacuum.
ASML of the Netherlands builds every EUV scanner in the world and shipped 48 of them in 2025.
EUV output is capped by Zeiss, which polishes the scanner's mirrors to within tens of picometers, so even ASML could not rebuild its supply quickly.
No EUV scanner has been sold to a customer in China, and China's answer is domestic immersion DUV plus an EUV prototype that has printed no chip.

quiz.q: Why do the finest layers of a leading-edge chip need an extreme-ultraviolet scanner?
options: EUV scanners work in open air, which keeps the wafer cool and flat during each exposure
EUV light passes through glass lenses more easily than the older deep ultraviolet light
EUV machines print every layer of a chip at once, which removes the need for masks
Light cannot draw a line much finer than its wavelength, and EUV light is the shortest
quiz.why: The finer the line, the shorter the light needed to print it. EUV light at 13.5 nm is stopped by glass and air, so the scanner works in a vacuum and uses mirrors.

quiz.q: How many companies build extreme-ultraviolet scanners?
options: None in volume yet, only prototypes
One, ASML of the Netherlands
Two, ASML and Nikon of Japan
Three, ASML, Nikon and Canon
quiz.why: ASML sold 48 EUV systems in 2025, and nobody else sells EUV. Nikon and Canon make deep ultraviolet scanners and steppers for coarser layers.

quiz.q: What caps how many EUV scanners ASML can build?
options: The supply of tin for the light source
Export licenses from the Dutch government
Zeiss polishing and coating of the mirrors
The number of engineers it can hire in San Diego
quiz.why: Zeiss makes the illumination system and the six-mirror projection optics, with mirrors up to a meter across. Final assembly in Veldhoven waits on those optics.

quiz.q: Where does China stand on EUV lithography?
options: A Shenzhen team has made EUV light, but no chip has been printed with it
Huawei has confirmed mass production of its own EUV scanners in 2026
SMEE sells small numbers of EUV scanners to Chinese foundries
Chinese foundries bought several EUV scanners from ASML before controls began
quiz.why: Reuters reported in December 2025 that a prototype makes extreme-ultraviolet light but no chip. No EUV scanner has ever been sold to a customer in China, and claims of Huawei mass production remain unverified.

takeaways: A photomask is the stencil for one layer of a chip, and the same plate prints that layer on wafer after wafer, so any flaw repeats on every wafer.
Three firms supply EUV mask blanks worldwide, led by AGC and Hoya of Japan, and only Lasertec of Japan sells a tool that inspects masks in EUV light.
The business is too small to fund a new entrant, which would face twenty years of defect learning to serve a handful of customers.
China has no EUV mask blank, no EUV inspection tool and no multi-beam writer, and SMIC's mask shops serve only older scanners.

quiz.q: Why must a photomask be free of defects?
options: Each mask is melted down and remade after it prints a single wafer
One plate prints its layer on wafer after wafer, repeating any flaw
A flawed mask damages the light source inside the scanner
Export rules require a defect report to be filed for each mask
quiz.why: One plate shapes millions of chips. A speck of dust or a buried particle prints on every wafer until someone finds it.

quiz.q: Which firm sells the only tool that inspects an EUV mask in the same light the scanner uses?
options: Lasertec
KLA
Zeiss
Photronics
quiz.why: Actinic inspection looks at 13.5 nm, the wavelength the mask itself sees, and Lasertec is the only supplier. KLA sells optical reticle inspection, and Zeiss sells e-beam repair.

quiz.q: Why has no new firm entered the market for EUV mask blanks?
options: Japanese law bars foreign firms from making mask blanks
ASML holds the patent on the forty-layer mirror coating
Blanks can be made only on EUV scanners, which are scarce
The market is too small to repay twenty years of defect learning
quiz.why: AGC aimed for more than ¥40 billion of annual sales in the business, serving a handful of customers. A business that small has kept the count of blank suppliers at three.

quiz.q: What mask-making capability does China have today?
options: EUV mask blanks made at home, with inspection done in Japan
Multi-beam writers made at home, with blanks bought from Japan
Masks for older scanners only, with no EUV blank or EUV inspection tool
No mask shops of its own, so every mask it uses arrives from Taiwan
quiz.why: SMIC runs two mask shops in Shanghai for g-line, i-line, KrF and ArF tools. No Chinese firm makes an EUV blank, an actinic inspection tool or a multi-beam writer.

takeaways: Deposition lays down films a few atoms thick and etch cuts away whatever the printed pattern leaves exposed, over more than a thousand steps per chip.
Applied Materials, Lam Research, Tokyo Electron and ASM International make most of these tools, and no single firm dominates as ASML does in lithography.
Most deposition and etch steps can be bought from three or four makers, but switching makers for the newest chips takes two to five years of testing.
Chinese makers reached about 11 percent of dry etch by 2024 and stayed under 1 percent of atomic layer deposition, which gate-all-around logic depends on.

quiz.q: How do deposition and etch work together to build a chip?
options: Etch grows the silicon crystal, and deposition slices it into wafers
Deposition prints the pattern, and etch checks whether it landed correctly
Deposition lays down a thin film, and etch removes what the pattern leaves exposed
Deposition cleans the wafer, and etch bonds the finished chips into packages
quiz.why: Deposition lays down a film a few atoms thick, lithography prints a pattern on it, and etch eats away what the pattern leaves unprotected. A chip takes more than a thousand of these rounds.

quiz.q: How does leadership in deposition and etch tools differ from leadership in lithography?
options: One Japanese firm makes every deposition and etch tool in use
Chinese firms hold most of the world market for these tools
Fabs design and build their own deposition and etch tools
Four firms share most of the market, and none dominates as ASML does
quiz.why: Applied Materials, Lam Research, Tokyo Electron and ASM International take most of the money. Each leads different tool families, such as Lam in conductor etch and ASM International in atomic layer deposition.

quiz.q: What does a fab face when it switches deposition or etch tool makers for its newest chips?
options: Two to five years of testing the new tool on its own line until it matches
A legal ban, because each fab may buy these tools from one maker only
A full redesign of the chip, since each tool maker needs its own masks
A few weeks of setup, since all deposition and etch tools are identical
quiz.why: Three or four credible makers exist for most deposition and etch steps. Switching still means testing the new tool on the fab's own line until it matches the old one.

quiz.q: In which kind of deposition and etch tool have Chinese makers gained least?
options: Dry etch
Atomic layer deposition
Deposition as a whole
Etch and clean
quiz.why: Between 2019 and 2024 China-based suppliers rose to about 11 percent of dry etch and 7 percent of deposition. In atomic layer deposition they gained nothing and stayed under 1 percent.

takeaways: Metrology and inspection tools check each wafer between steps for line width, layer alignment and defects, which is how a fab learns why its chips fail.
KLA of the United States holds about 57 percent of the process control tool market, six to seven times its nearest rival, and its share is still growing.
A bigger chip is a bigger target for a stray speck, so AI accelerators, among the largest chips cut from a wafer, depend most on finding defects.
Chinese firms held 0.7 percent of the process control tool market in 2025, their weakest position in any major kind of chipmaking tool.

quiz.q: What do metrology and inspection tools do in a fab?
options: They check the wafer between steps for line width, alignment and defects
They lay down the thin films that form each new layer of the chip
They print the circuit pattern onto the wafer with a beam of light
They cut the finished wafer into separate chips ready for packaging
quiz.why: Between the steps that build a chip, these tools look the wafer over. They measure line widths and the overlay between layers and find stray defects, so the fab can learn why chips fail.

quiz.q: How does KLA's position compare with its rivals in process control tools?
options: It is one of five firms with roughly equal shares of the market
It leads only in critical dimension metrology, and trails elsewhere
It holds about 57 percent, six to seven times its nearest rival
It lost its lead to ASML after 2021 and now ranks second
quiz.why: CSET puts KLA at 56.8 percent of a $15.7 billion market in 2025, and KLA says its share is still rising. Nobody else reaches 11 percent.

quiz.q: Why does finding defects matter more for AI accelerators than for small chips?
options: AI accelerators are made on older equipment that leaves more defects
Export rules require every AI chip to be inspected twice before sale
AI chips are printed without masks, so each one has to be checked
Their chips are among the largest, and a bigger chip is a bigger target
quiz.why: Yield loss grows faster than chip area. For an 8 square centimeter die, halving the defect density lifts yield from about 49 percent to about 69 percent.

quiz.q: Where do Chinese toolmakers stand in metrology and inspection?
options: They lead the world in critical dimension measurement
It is the major kind of tool where they are weakest
They match KLA in defect inspection for mature chips
They supply most of the inspection tools in Chinese fabs
quiz.why: Chinese firms held 0.7 percent of the process control tool market in 2025. Without sensitive inspection, a fab cannot find out why its yield is low.

takeaways: The front end builds the transistors, and wrapping the gate around all four sides of each channel stops current leaking when the switch is off.
Only TSMC, Intel and Samsung can build 2 nm-class gate-all-around transistors, and only TSMC runs such a process at volume for outside customers.
The scarce asset is the process recipe, meaning which steps run in which order on which tools, and no firm sells its recipe.
SMIC reaches 5 nm-class features without EUV by printing each layer in several passes, which still leaves China behind the newest chips.

quiz.q: Why do the newest transistors wrap the gate around all four sides of the channel?
options: To let the chip run without any wiring layers above the transistors
To shut the flow fully, since a short channel leaks when the gate is off
To let older scanners print the transistor in a single exposure
To replace the silicon channel with a cheaper strip of metal
quiz.why: A shorter channel switches faster and packs tighter, but it leaks current even when the gate is off. A gate on every side can squeeze the flow shut.

quiz.q: Which companies can build a 2 nm-class gate-all-around transistor?
options: TSMC, SMIC and Rapidus
Intel, SMIC and Samsung
TSMC, Samsung and Rapidus
TSMC, Intel and Samsung
quiz.why: TSMC, Intel and Samsung build gate-all-around nodes with extreme ultraviolet lithography. SMIC builds 7 and 5 nm-class nodes without it, and Rapidus targets 2 nm mass production in 2027.

quiz.q: What makes the front end a chokepoint?
options: A single machine that only one firm in the world can build
A rare metal for the gate that is mined in only one country
The recipe of which steps run in which order on which tools
A patent on the nanosheet transistor held by a single firm
quiz.why: No single machine makes the front end a chokepoint. Three firms have written a recipe for the newest transistors, none sells it, and a newcomer has to work out its own.

quiz.q: How does SMIC reach 5 nm-class features without an extreme-ultraviolet scanner?
options: It prints each layer in several passes on deep-ultraviolet tools
It licenses the recipe for TSMC's N2 process through a partner
It buys used EUV scanners from fabs in Taiwan and South Korea
It makes each chip larger so the features never have to shrink
quiz.why: SMIC gets fine features from deep-ultraviolet machines by printing each layer in several passes. CSIS judges that China still cannot build a working EUV system.

takeaways: A foundry makes chips for other companies on shared tools, because no chip company sells enough of one product to fill a fab costing tens of billions of dollars.
TSMC leads the foundries, and all six of its largest plants, which hold 13 of its 17 million wafers a year, are in Taiwan.
Money can buy a fab building, and the slow part is a workforce that has run one process for years, so a working line takes five to ten years.
China has the most fab capacity of any region, almost none of it advanced, and Intel is the only American-owned foundry making the newest chips.

quiz.q: Why do chip companies share foundries instead of each building its own fab?
options: Governments forbid chip designers from owning any factories
Only foundries are allowed to buy lithography scanners
Each design needs tools from every country to be made
No single company sells enough of one product to fill a fab
quiz.why: A fab costs tens of billions of dollars, and BCG puts the ten-year cost of one finished in 2026 at $35 to $43 billion. A foundry runs many customers' designs through the same tools by recipe.

quiz.q: Where are TSMC's six largest plants, the gigafabs?
options: All six are in Taiwan
Three in Taiwan and three in Arizona
Four in Taiwan, one in Japan, one in China
Split between Taiwan and Kumamoto
quiz.why: Each gigafab runs more than 100,000 wafers a month. Together they hold 13 of TSMC's 17 million wafers a year, and Arizona, Kumamoto, Nanjing and Washington hold the rest.

quiz.q: What makes moving leading-edge chipmaking out of Taiwan slow?
options: Scanners may not legally be shipped outside Taiwan
Building a workforce that has run one process for years
The price of land for new fabs in the United States
A shortage of silicon wafers in factories outside Asia
quiz.why: Money can buy the building. Training the workforce is the slow part, and TSMC has yet to build a gigafab anywhere but Taiwan despite committing $165 billion to the United States.

quiz.q: Which description fits China's foundry capacity?
options: Small in volume, but mostly at the leading edge
Larger than Taiwan's, and mostly at 2 nm and 3 nm
The most of any region, with almost none of it advanced
Shrinking fast as its fabs move to Southeast Asia
quiz.why: SEMI forecast China at 10.1 million wafers a month in 2025, against Taiwan's 5.8 million. SMIC cannot buy an EUV scanner, so almost none of that capacity makes the newest chips.

takeaways: HBM stacks memory chips into a cube wired through copper-filled holes, and its speed and size usually set how many users one AI chip can serve.
SK hynix, Samsung and Micron make every HBM stack in the world, and the two Korean firms sold 82.5 percent of it in 2025.
A new HBM maker would need the newest DRAM and a line that thins and stacks chips without warping, then pass Nvidia's test, which takes five to ten years.
A US export control catches every HBM stack now in production, and CXMT, China's HBM maker, remains behind the three leaders.

quiz.q: Why does memory speed matter so much when an AI chip answers a prompt?
options: The chip has to rewrite its own circuit design before it gives each answer
Answering a prompt uses far more arithmetic per number than training does
For each word, the chip reads the whole model from memory and does little arithmetic
HBM stores the electricity that the chip draws to produce each answer
quiz.why: To generate each word the chip reads the whole model and the record of the conversation, then waits for the next read. Memory size and speed usually set how many people one chip can serve.

quiz.q: Which firms make every HBM stack in the world?
options: SK hynix, Samsung and CXMT
SK hynix, Samsung and Micron
Samsung, Micron and TSMC
Micron, SK hynix and Intel
quiz.why: SK hynix took 63.2 percent of 2025 HBM revenue, Samsung 19.3 and Micron 17.4. TSMC builds the logic base die for SK hynix's HBM4 and makes no stacks itself.

quiz.q: What would a fourth HBM maker need inside one company?
options: A license from JEDEC to use the HBM4 standard
A foundry able to make 2 nm logic chips
An EUV scanner set aside for stacking memory
Leading-edge DRAM and a line that thins and stacks chips
quiz.why: Nobody outside the three has both leading-edge DRAM and a stacking line inside one company. The finished stack then has to pass Nvidia's qualification test.

quiz.q: Why does the US export control on HBM leave no compliant high-end stack to sell into China?
options: Its bandwidth-density threshold catches every stack now in production
It bans every kind of memory export to China, including ordinary DRAM
It applies only to HBM stacks that are made inside the United States
It sets a price cap that makes every sale of HBM unprofitable
quiz.why: ECCN 3A090.c covers HBM above 2 gigabytes per second per square millimeter, and every stack in production exceeds it. The rule also reaches stacks made abroad with American technology.

takeaways: An AI accelerator needs more circuit than a scanner prints in one shot, so packaging joins several chips and their memory on a shared silicon interposer.
TSMC packages nearly every AI accelerator with its CoWoS process in Taiwan, and Nvidia alone took an estimated 60.3 percent of CoWoS in 2025.
Each packaging step is ordinary on its own, and the hard part is making enough working packages at volume, which capped AI chip output in 2024 and 2025.
China packages chips at scale but has no silicon-interposer packaging at volume, and American CoWoS-class capacity starts only in 2028.

quiz.q: Why is an AI accelerator built from several chips in one package?
options: It needs more circuit than a scanner can print in one exposure
Export rules for AI parts require the logic to be split up
Each chip in it has to come from a different foundry
A single large chip cannot be cooled by any known method
quiz.why: A scanner prints a rectangle of 858 mm2 in one exposure. Packaging sets the pieces and their memory side by side on a silicon interposer and wires them together.

quiz.q: Which firm packages nearly every leading AI accelerator?
options: Amkor
JCET
ASE Technology
TSMC
quiz.why: TSMC does the 2.5D work with its CoWoS process in its own back-end fabs in Taiwan. Outsourced firms such as ASE, Amkor and JCET handle the rest of the packaging market.

quiz.q: Why did packaging cap AI chip output through 2024 and 2025?
options: The steps needed physics that no firm had yet worked out
The physics was solved, and too few lines had been built
Export controls kept the bonding tools out of Taiwan
Memory makers held back HBM from the packaging lines
quiz.why: Each packaging step is ordinary on its own, but one cracked joint scraps a whole package. Four designers absorbed around 90 percent of CoWoS, and by March 2026 the constraint had moved back to front-end wafers.

quiz.q: Where do China and the United States stand in AI-class packaging?
options: China leads in silicon interposers, and the United States in bonding tools
Both countries already run CoWoS-class packaging lines at volume
China lacks interposer packaging at volume, and US capacity starts in 2028
The United States packages most accelerators, and China makes the interposers
quiz.why: JCET billed RMB 35.96 billion in 2024, yet China has no silicon-interposer 2.5D at volume with qualified HBM beside it. Amkor's plant in Peoria, Arizona starts production in early 2028.

takeaways: A package substrate is the layered adapter that carries signals from a chip's hair-fine connections down to a circuit board wired in millimeters.
Ajinomoto of Japan puts its share of the insulating film inside high-end packages at about 95 percent, and Nitto Boseki of Japan leads in the glass cloth beneath it.
Money can expand substrate plants, and a replacement film would still need approval in each layer of each product at every substrate maker, which takes five to ten years.
No American firm makes these substrates in volume, and Chinese firms make almost none of the high-end film, though they are pushing into glass cloth.

quiz.q: What job does a package substrate do?
options: It cools the chip by drawing heat down into the circuit board
It stores data for the processor between its calculations
It holds the stencil used to print each of the chip's layers
It links the chip's fine connections to a board wired in millimeters
quiz.why: The substrate is built up in layers of epoxy film and copper around a stiff glass-cloth core. Its layers spread the chip's hair-fine connections out to the coarser board.

quiz.q: Which company makes most of the insulating film inside high-end chip packages?
options: Ajinomoto
Ibiden
Unimicron
Samsung Electro-Mechanics
quiz.why: Ajinomoto, a Japanese food company, puts its share of the film at about 95 percent, and its film has been the standard since 1999. Ibiden, Unimicron and Samsung Electro-Mechanics build substrates that use it.

quiz.q: Why would replacing Ajinomoto's film take five to ten years?
options: Only one factory in the world is able to make epoxy film of any kind
A Japanese export ban keeps the film recipe from leaving the country
Every substrate maker must approve a new film in each layer of each product
The film has to be grown slowly as a single crystal over many months
quiz.why: A newcomer can build a line to make the film. Every substrate maker and packaging house then has to approve it layer by layer, and that takes years at each of them.

quiz.q: Where do the United States and China stand in package substrates?
options: The United States leads in build-up film, and China in substrate plants
China makes little high-end film, and no US firm makes substrates in volume
China makes most of the high-end film, and the United States the glass cloth
Both run large substrate plants that ship directly to the leading GPU makers
quiz.why: None of the eight substrate makers named in the 2021 White House supply chain review is American, and Chinese firms make almost none of the high-end film. Nitto Boseki names Chinese firms as fast followers in special glass.

takeaways: Test puts electricity through each chip at several stages, so a bad die is caught before it can ruin a package holding a dozen expensive pieces.
Advantest of Japan sold about 65 percent of chip testers in 2025, and together with Teradyne of the United States it holds about 80 percent.
Every test and assembly tool has more than one maker, and switching testers is slow because it means rebuilding every test program.
Assembly and test is where China is strongest, with four of the top ten assembly and test firms, because the export controls leave these tools uncovered.

quiz.q: Why does the industry now test chips sooner, hotter and longer than it used to?
options: Export rules require each AI chip to be tested three separate times
One bad die can ruin a package holding a dozen expensive pieces
Testers have become cheaper to run than the chips they check
Chips printed on EUV scanners fail far more often than older chips
quiz.why: An accelerator joins many costly dies, and one weak piece scraps them all. Wafer sort, burn-in, final test and system-level test each catch failures the round before cannot see.

quiz.q: Which firm sells about two thirds of the world's chip testers?
options: Teradyne
Disco
Advantest
FormFactor
quiz.why: Advantest puts its share at about 65 percent of a $9.0 billion tester market in 2025. With Teradyne, the second maker, it holds about 80 percent.

quiz.q: Why do chip customers rarely switch tester makers?
options: A new tester means rebuilding the test program for each product
Each tester maker holds a patent on the chips its machines test
Testers are built into the fab walls and cannot be moved out
Export law ties each chip customer to a single tester maker
quiz.why: Advantest argues that switching means rebuilding the whole development, evaluation and production test setup. Share therefore moves slowly even though no tool has a single maker.

quiz.q: Why do export controls have little effect on assembly and test?
options: Most assembly and test already takes place inside the United States
Assembly and test firms work by hand and need no machines at all
China buys all of its test machines from firms in Malaysia
These tools fall outside the controls, and China has strong firms
quiz.why: Assembly, dicing, bonding and test tools are not covered by the controls on lithography and deposition. CSET counts four of the top ten assembly and test firms by 2024 revenue as Chinese.

takeaways: AI chips are wired into racks of 72 that run as one computer, with copper links inside each rack and lasers sending light down glass fiber beyond it.
Rack assembly is competitive, and if Foxconn stopped, Quanta and Wistron could take over its volume within a few quarters.
The hard parts to replace are NVLink-class switching, which only Nvidia sells at that bandwidth, and the indium phosphide lasers for the optical links.
American firms make the switch chips and lasers, while Chinese firms assemble high-speed optical modules in volume and China produces about 70 percent of the world's indium.

quiz.q: Why do the longer links in an AI cluster send signals as light down glass fiber?
options: Glass fiber costs less to install than any kind of copper cable
Export rules forbid copper links between racks of AI chips
Copper carries these signals only a few meters before they fade
Light lets each chip skip the memory stacks beside it
quiz.why: Inside a rack the trays reach each other over copper. Beyond it every link runs on glass fiber, with a laser at one end turning the electrical signal into pulses of light.

quiz.q: What would happen if Foxconn stopped assembling AI racks?
options: Quanta and Wistron would take over the volume within a few quarters
No AI racks could be built anywhere in the world for several years
Nvidia would have to assemble every rack in plants of its own
Rack assembly would move entirely to China within a month
quiz.why: Several contract manufacturers on three continents build racks, and the power shelves, busbars, cables and connectors have many suppliers. Assembly is the easiest part of this stage to replace.

quiz.q: Which parts of an AI rack are hardest to replace?
options: The steel frames and the cable trays
The power shelves and copper busbars
The cooling pipes and the building loop
NVLink-class switching and indium phosphide lasers
quiz.why: Nobody else sells a scale-up switch with NVLink's bandwidth to all comers, which UALink aims to change. Nvidia put $2 billion each into Coherent and Lumentum to secure laser capacity.

quiz.q: Where does China hold a strong position in AI networking?
options: Its firms design the fastest Ethernet switch chips sold to all comers
It assembles optical modules in volume and produces most of the world's indium
It controls the NVLink standard through a licensing deal with Nvidia
Its firms make most of the indium phosphide lasers in their Taiwan plants
quiz.why: InnoLight and Eoptolink assemble high-speed optical modules in China and Thailand, and China accounts for about 70 percent of world indium production. American firms make the switch chips and the lasers.

takeaways: A data center feeds power to its racks and carries their heat away, and one AI rack draws up to 142 kilowatts, more heat than air can remove.
Power equipment now sets the pace of a buildout, and a large power transformer takes about 36 months to arrive, against under a year before 2020.
Several vendors sell every piece of power and cooling equipment, so money buys the gear, and it cannot shorten the queues for transformers and turbines.
The United States has the demand and the money but imports most large power transformers, while China has spare generating capacity and is limited by accelerators.

quiz.q: Why are new AI racks cooled with water?
options: Water cooling lets a rack run without any power shelves
Regulators require liquid cooling in every new building
Water is cheaper to move than air through large halls
A 142 kW rack gives off more heat than air can carry away
quiz.why: Every watt a rack draws comes back out as heat. Cold plates on the GPU packages pass it to a building water loop that releases it outdoors.

quiz.q: How long does a large power transformer now commonly take to arrive?
options: About 6 months
About 36 months
About 12 months
About 10 years
quiz.why: Thirty-six-month lead times are commonly quoted and the worst reach 60, against under a year before the pandemic. Every announced campus waits in that queue.

quiz.q: What can money not buy quickly in a data center buildout?
options: A shorter wait for transformers and gas turbines
Cooling equipment from an approved vendor
A design for an 800-volt power system
Liquid cold plates for the GPU packages
quiz.why: Nvidia names nine firms that supply power and cooling systems for its gigawatt designs, so buyers can get that equipment. GE Vernova has close to six years of gas turbine output booked.

quiz.q: How do China and the United States differ in powering AI data centers?
options: China lacks power, and the United States lacks accelerators
Both are held back mainly by a shortage of cooling equipment
China has spare power, and the United States waits years for equipment
The United States exports most of its transformers to China
quiz.why: China has spare generating capacity and its own transformer and switchgear industry, so accelerators limit its buildout. The United States imported 82 percent of the large power transformers it put into service in 2019.

takeaways: Building a Blackwell B200 costs about $6,400, and Nvidia sells it for $30,000 to $40,000.
High-bandwidth memory is the largest line in the build, about 45 percent, while the logic dies are about 14 percent.
Packaging and its scrap cost more than twice the logic dies, because a package that fails after the memory goes on throws away the dies and the memory.
The costliest parts are the scarcest, with three firms making the memory and one Taiwanese firm doing the packaging, and in 2026 Micron's gross margin passed Nvidia's.

quiz.q: What does a Blackwell B200 cost to build, and what does it sell for?
options: About $900 to build, sold for about $6,400
About $6,400 to build, sold for $30,000 to $40,000
About $17,000 to build, sold for about $30,000
About $30,000 to build, sold for about $40,000
quiz.why: Epoch AI puts the build at about $6,400, within a range of $5,700 to $7,300. About $900 of that is the two logic dies.

quiz.q: Which line is the largest in the cost of building a B200?
options: The two logic dies from TSMC
Packaging yield loss
The high-bandwidth memory
Substrate, board and test
quiz.why: The 192 GB of HBM3E costs about $2,900, 45 percent of the build. Three firms make that memory, and they sell every stack they can build.

quiz.q: Why does packaging yield add so much to the cost of a B200?
options: Each failed package has to be shipped back from the customer
Packaging runs on wafers larger than those for the logic dies
Failed packages are sold at a steep discount to smaller buyers
A package that fails after the memory goes on scraps dies and memory
quiz.why: Packaging yield runs 65 to 95 percent. Scrap adds roughly $1,000 to every B200 that ships, on top of about $1,100 for CoWoS-L packaging itself.

quiz.q: Where did the highest reported gross margin in the chain sit in 2026?
options: With the memory maker Micron, ahead of Nvidia
With TSMC, ahead of every chip designer
With ASML, the only maker of EUV scanners
With assembly and test firms such as ASE
quiz.why: Micron reported an 84.6 percent gross margin in the quarter to May 2026, against 75.0 percent at Nvidia. Assembly and test firms earned 17 to 21 percent.

takeaways: An export control works only when a country's own firms sell something the buyer cannot get elsewhere, which is why a few countries can use one on chips.
Since 2020 Washington has built its controls one rule at a time, reaching foreign goods made with US technology and, from 2022, whole countries.
The controls have kept China below the leading edge, and Chinese tool vendors still took 35 percent of their home market in 2025.
Taiwan holds 78 percent of the world's contract chipmaking, and no policy so far has moved leading-edge logic or packaging off the island.

quiz.q: When does an export control have real effect?
options: When the country's own firms sell something the buyer cannot get elsewhere
When the controlling country buys more chips than any other country
When the World Trade Organization has approved the rule in advance
When the buyer's own government agrees to enforce the rule itself
quiz.why: The machines, software and chemicals for an advanced chip come from a short list of firms in the United States, the Netherlands, Japan and South Korea. That short list is what gives those governments a hold over buyers.

quiz.q: What did the Foreign Direct Product Rule of August 2020 change?
options: It barred US persons from servicing advanced Chinese fabs
It put a 25 percent tariff on advanced chips from Taiwan
It capped exportable AI chips by processing performance
It reached foreign items made with US technology and bound for Huawei
quiz.why: Huawei had turned to foreign chips after its 2019 Entity List listing. Extending the rule to foreign items made with US technology made American controls extraterritorial.
quiz.section: The US export-control campaign, 2018 to today

quiz.q: Where has Chinese substitution succeeded, and where has it stalled?
options: It has succeeded in EUV machines and stalled in mature-node chips
It has succeeded in HBM and stalled in etch and deposition tools
It has succeeded in domestic tools and stalled at the leading edge
It has succeeded in EUV resist and stalled in DRAM and NAND
quiz.why: Chinese tool vendors took 35 percent of their home market in 2025. SMIC still prints 7 nm-class logic without an EUV scanner, and a shortage of memory stacks caps Ascend output.

quiz.q: What has industrial policy done to Taiwan's lead in leading-edge chipmaking so far?
options: Moved most 2 nm production to Arizona during 2025
Left 2 nm running only in Taiwan, with Arizona a generation behind
Shifted advanced packaging to Japan through Rapidus
Split leading-edge output evenly between Taiwan and Korea
quiz.why: Taiwan's foundries hold 78 percent of contract chipmaking on the 2025 industry count, and 2 nm runs nowhere else. Taiwan bars overseas production of its most advanced chips, so TSMC's American fabs run a generation behind.
